entries.label: Two
entries.ambiguity: The invariant is the number of marks. The repeated arrangement could instead suggest a pair, symmetry, or equal spacing.

entries.label: Inside
entries.ambiguity: A closed boundary contains a mark in each positive example. A 2D diagram cannot by itself distinguish containment from projected overlap.

entries.label: Change of position
entries.ambiguity: Successive frames suggest one object changing position. A reader may see separate objects or infer the reverse order. Frame order depends on the primer.

entries.label: Earth
entries.ambiguity: The two views show the same planet from different perspectives. The shared shape may suggest the class of planets instead of this individual body.

entries.label: Plant
entries.ambiguity: The fern and tree show two examples of plants. Backgrounds and different scales make it unclear which pictured feature carries the label.

entries.label: Human
entries.ambiguity: Groups in varied settings show multiple humans. The examples cannot independently teach species membership, cultural roles, or the range of human variation.

statements.label: Two inside
statements.ambiguity: The trial convention places quantity before relationship. The sequence alone leaves the object type and enclosing boundary implicit.

statements.label: Two move
statements.ambiguity: These examples hold the number constant as positions change. They do not establish tense, agency, cause or simultaneous movement.
